implement.summary:
Defect on BASE_SHA d8e5db3e (VERIFIED by the failing regression test, INFERRED from code): the scored settlement's idempotent replay was keyed on (owner, shot id) only — supabase/functions/api/index.ts:2065-2104 (`replayIds` from `select id from shots where user_id = uid and id in (...)` → `acceptedIds.push`) and the RPC's pre-lock/under-lock `exists(select 1 from public.shots where id = ... and user_id = ...)` replay in supabase/migrations/20260908100000_permit_partial_terminal_outcome.sql. No receipt was persisted or returned; device/grant/ticket/operation claims were not parsed (parseSyncShot ignored them, index.ts:1790-1950); the payload digest from canonicalDigest.ts and the verified release-policy lineage (releasePolicy.ts VerifiedReleasePolicy) were not bound to the settlement. Consequently a different payload/permit/device replayed under the same shot id was 'accepted' as a replay, and nothing let a client or auditor prove which settlement a shot id denotes.

Fix (all inside write_paths + one justified test-harness edit): (1) supabase/migrations/20260908110000_settlement_receipt_lineage.sql — new `public.settlement_receipts` (shot_id PK→shots cascade, user_id→profiles cascade, denormalized binding columns with shape CHECKs, receipt jsonb + canonical bytes + sha256; RLS on, owner SELECT through the api_private.is_api_request() restrictive gate only, no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, append-only trigger for every role) and `apply_synced_shot(jsonb)` recreated to require a well-formed `shot.settlementReceipt` {canonical, sha256} whose bytes hash to the digest and whose binding names this shot/owner/permit/resultKind (else 'shot.receipt_invalid'), require policy lineage for scored, decide replay on binding + policy lineage both BEFORE the per-user advisory lock and again under it — identical → 'accepted' (original stands, nothing moves), any difference → 'shot.receipt_mismatch' — before the permit, free-rating backstop, ledger or shot are touched; existing permit lifecycle, lifetime_scored_count() under access_lock_key(), SQLSTATE mapping and generic errors preserved. (2) supabase/functions/api/index.ts — `parseSettlementClaims` (installationKeyId / grant{grantId, grantJwsSha256} / ticket{allocationId, generation, ticketId} / operationId; omitted ⇒ all null, present ⇒ exact shape or per-shot 'shot.invalid_payload'), `SettlementBinding` with `payloadSha256 = digestCanonicalOfflineJson(shot)` (canonicalDigest.ts, unchanged), `settlementPolicyLineage(VerifiedReleasePolicy)` (version, policy sha256, validFrom/Until, mechanics+benchmark lineage, approval timestamps/withdrawal/deny flag), receipt = canonical bytes + sha256; syncShots reads the owner's stored receipts in one batched owner-scoped SELECT beside the shots SELECT, returns the ORIGINAL stored receipt for an identical binding (no authority read, no RPC), rejects a mismatched binding as 'shot.receipt_mismatch' before the authority read and the RPC, treats a stored receipt that fails byte/digest/canonical verification as retryable 'shot.write_failed' via the existing operator sink (never fabricated into a replay), and returns `receipts: [{id, canonical, sha256}]` in the acknowledgement only when a settlement carries one (the mobile decoder tolerates the extra key; the existing exact-shape test for an all-rejected batch is untouched). (3) supabase/tests/security_regression.sql — section T (T1–T7) + K24 inventory row. (4) supabase/functions/api/__wf__/xc_concurrency_harness.ts — models the new table (out_of_scope_files).

blocking_issues: supabase/migrations/20260908110000_settlement_receipt_lineage.sql:128-152 (guard_settlement_receipt_lifecycle + trigger settlement_receipts_lifecycle BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE): the append-only guard allows a DELETE only when `not exists (select 1 from public.shots where id = old.shot_id)`. settlement_receipts has TWO cascade parents (shot_id → shots ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id → profiles ON DELETE CASCADE) and shots.user_id also cascades from profiles. When a profile is deleted (auth.users → profiles account-deletion cascade), PostgreSQL fires the two RI cascade triggers on profiles in trigger-NAME order (`RI_ConstraintTrigger_a_<oid>`), which is not a guaranteed ordering. If the settlement_receipts_user_id_fkey cascade fires BEFORE the shots_user_id_fkey cascade, the receipt is deleted while its shot still exists and the guard RAISEs `settlement_receipts: a receipt outlives every path but the shot cascade` — account deletion fails for every user who owns a receipted shot. REPRODUCED on the candidate DB (reviewer probe, rolled back): artifacts/review-w01-03/probe_cascade_order.sql — creates a user/profile/permit/shot/receipt, recreates shots_user_id_fkey so its RI trigger name sorts after the receipts one, then `delete from auth.users where id = ...` → `ERROR: settlement_receipts: a receipt outlives every path but the shot cascade / CONTEXT: guard_settlement_receipt_lifecycle() line 9 / SQL statement DELETE FROM ONLY public.settlement_receipts WHERE $1 = user_id` (log: https://la-hacks-rttothemoon.devinenterprise.com/attachments/87ad9402-b20c-4d17-9713-0ba3a3725b17/probe_cascade_order.log , probe: https://la-hacks-rttothemoon.devinenterprise.com/attachments/0a405b1e-bcc9-4562-bca1-1f3f5f980fd0/probe_cascade_order.sql ). T7 and the W08 matrix pass in the test histories only because in a fresh cluster the older shots FK has a numerically-and-lexically smaller OID; in production the shots_user_id_fkey OID is fixed and the new FK's OID is whatever the deploy allocates — if the two OIDs differ in digit count (e.g. 9xxxx vs 1xxxxx) the lexical order flips (production ordering UNKNOWN; cannot be inspected per the no-production rule). The repo's own precedent for a delete guard on a doubly-cascaded table handles exactly this: guard_analysis_permit_delete in 20260907100000_permit_settled_no_delete.sql:129-134 first checks `not exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = old.user_id)` (account cascade → allow). Fix (new later-timestamped migration, not an edit): make guard_settlement_receipt_lifecycle also return old when the owning profile row is gone (or drop the redundant user_id ON DELETE CASCADE so only the shot cascade removes receipts), and add a matrix case that exercises the cascade with the receipts FK trigger firing first.
non_blocking_issues: supabase/migrations/20260908110000_settlement_receipt_lineage.sql:~522-539 (`when unique_violation` fallback in apply_synced_shot): the replay comparison there checks binding_sha256 + binding but omits the `(v_stored.receipt -> 'policy') is not distinct from (v_receipt -> 'policy')` term that the pre-lock/under-lock replay path (lines ~389-408) applies. INFERRED unreachable for a policy-only mismatch in practice: same-owner settlements are serialized by pg_advisory_xact_lock(access_lock_key(uid)) and READ COMMITTED re-reads the committed row in attempt 2, so the fallback only fires for a row inserted outside the RPC (which has no receipt → 'accepted', as legacy). Should be made identical to the primary check for consistency.

Shots settled before 20260908110000 have no receipt; their replay keeps the prior ownership-only verdict (Edge index.ts ~2349-2352 `if (!row) { if (replayIds.has(id)) accepted }` and RPC `if not found then return 'accepted'`). Acknowledged by the implementer as residual risk; a mismatched replay of a pre-receipt shot is not detectable. Acceptable as compatibility for already-settled rows (no credit can be consumed on that path), but should be recorded in the release packet.

Deploy ordering: the Edge `settlement_receipts` SELECT fails closed (PGRST205 → generic 503, retryable) until 20260908110000 is applied, so `supabase db push` must precede `functions deploy api` or every shot sync 503s in the interval.

Shipping mobile client does not yet send `settlement` claims (all-null, recorded as absent) nor consume `receipts`; device/grant/ticket/operation binding is end-to-end only after the client packages wire them. packages/api-contracts ShotsSyncResponse does not list the optional `receipts` key (zod strips unknown keys; mobile decoder verified tolerant in apps/mobile/src/data/api.ts).

Prior-round P0 resolved: the r1 lifecycle guard (20260908110000_settlement_receipt_lineage.sql:128-152) admitted a DELETE only when the shot was already gone; settlement_receipts has two cascade parents (shot_id→shots, user_id→profiles) and shots cascades from profiles, and PostgreSQL fires same-event RI cascade triggers on profiles in trigger-NAME order (RI_ConstraintTrigger_a_<oid>, text compare), so with the receipts FK's oid sorting first the receipt cascade reached the row while its shot still existed and account deletion raised 23514 for every owner with a settled shot. Fix: NEW migration supabase/migrations/20260908120000_settlement_receipt_account_cascade.sql replaces guard_settlement_receipt_lifecycle() to return old when the owning profile row is already gone (account cascade, same detection as guard_analysis_permit_delete) OR when the shot is gone (shot cascade), still raising while both exist; UPDATE stays refused; no grant/policy/trigger changes; 20260908110000 untouched. Matrix: security_regression.sql T8a/T8b force each profiles-cascade order (recreate the other FK → newer oid, assert order from pg_trigger, settle via apply_synced_shot, delete auth.users → profile+shot+receipt gone, no error), T8c pins that a receipt with a live shot and owner remains undeletable.
